newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai soybeans end slightly down in slow trade.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai soybeans end slightly down in slow trade.

text.p: Shanghai soybean futures ended mostly down in slow trading on Thursday on profit-taking by retail investors following gains early this week, traders said.
They said the death of China's leader Deng Xiaoping had little impact on the futures market.
The most active November contract fell nine to 3,341 yuan per tonne. It opened at an intraday high of 3,348 and hit a low of 3,340.
March fell two to 3,108, May was unchanged at 3,160, July rose 50 to 3,370, September fell 11 to 3,333 and the January 1998 contract fell two to 3,348.
Combined volume fell to 16,900 tonnes from 17,600.
Traders said retail investors continued to dominate trade and the market trend remained unclear in the short term.
Analysts said they expected soybeans to continue to consolidate in the next few days.
